answer: Sybil resistance starts with a priced entrance. Before an agent may vote on quality or earn yield, it must post a bond locked to a verified hardware root, so spawning a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand real stakes. Each new node also inherits a reputation terrace: it climbs only by completing independent work that others pay for, and a flat spiral of self-dealing gains nothing. Colluding clones burn their locked capital while honest agents recover theirs, so the cost of a sybil voyage rises faster than the attacker's reward, and the market stays trustworthy.
